### Observed differences

- Activity A02 became less frequent: in the earlier window it appeared in about 27 in 100 traces (53 of 200) with roughly 0.3 occurrences per trace, while in the later window it appeared in about 15 in 100 traces (30 of 200) with about 0.16 occurrences per trace — a drop of about 0.135 occurrences per trace. [OCC001]
- The decline comes mainly from fewer traces containing A02 at all: repeats of A02 within a single trace were rare in both windows (recurrence support about 3 in 100 traces earlier and about 1 in 100 later). [OCC001]
- The size of the drop is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data, so it is unusual for an unchanged process, but it rests on a single indicator out of 87 tested units. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one item qualified, which is what an unchanged process typically produces here (about 0.43 items expected by chance across the 87 tested units), so the apparent drop in A02 participation could reflect sampling variation between the two windows despite its high empirical strength. [OCC001]
